lines.en: Han Sooyoung and Yoo Joonghyuk were carried on stretchers and admitted to the hospital where Kim Dokja lay.

As Lee Seolhwa gave her a thorough scolding, Han Sooyoung calmly organized the plans in her head. Exactly an hour later, she explained them to the others, using the most precise words she could and sentences without leaps in logic.
But a precise explanation does not guarantee that its listeners will understand it precisely. And so the companions reacted as follows.
“······You want to do what?”
Jung Heewon asked again, while Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung's mouths fell slightly open.
Han Sooyoung spoke.
“So, to put it simply······.”
“You do know what you're saying right now?”
“······Huh? You understood?”
“We can't do something like that again. Have you already forgotten what happened two years ago? What happened to us during Group Regression······.”
“I'm not saying we should regress.”
“Same difference! If we cross worldlines again―”
“I'm not saying we should twist another worldline's future. You know what I mean. All we're doing is taking a novel over there.”
Lee Jihye, who had listened silently, spoke.
“So we're showing the Dokja-ajusshi in another worldline a novel we wrote here? Did I get that right?”
“Right.”
“What good would that do?”
Han Sooyoung began explaining calmly.
“The 'Oldest Dream' is Kim Dokja. And that Kim Dokja shattered into tiny pieces, scattered across the worldlines, and reincarnated as other beings. You understand that much?”
“······You think I'm an actual idiot just because I got a few Fs? And?”

“Here's the important part. The reincarnated Kim Dokjas might no longer be 'Kim Dokja'. But that doesn't mean they aren't the 'Oldest Dream' anymore. They don't know it themselves, but those souls are still the 'Oldest Dream' maintaining this universe.”
When they had finally escaped the [Final Wall], no one had remained on the subway. Yet the universe's time had not stopped. In other words, the 'Oldest Dream' had not disappeared.
The souls that had once been Kim Dokja had now scattered throughout the universe and reincarnated. Wherever they were reborn, they were dreaming of these universes without knowing it.
Yoo Sangah nodded as though she understood.
“You mean to use their imagination.”
“Whatever the Oldest Dream imagines becomes reality.”
“Have the reincarnations of Dokja-ssi dream of the ending we want······.”
“Exactly. We provide the source for their imagination. So they can dream of this world's ending.”
Han Sooyoung looked at each companion's face as she spoke.
“No one will get hurt. We won't hurt anyone born in another worldline. We just have to get them to read a certain story.”
She imagined the countless Kim Dokjas scattered across worldlines. People who must have been born in different circumstances, in different forms.
Meeting them or bringing them back meant nothing now.
All the companions could hope for now was a miracle.
A miracle that would bring back the Kim Dokja they remembered.
Even if it was fiction. Even if it was a lie. If only he would imagine his own happiness.
If all those 'Kim Dokjas' would imagine a single universe.
Silence settled briefly. Similar expressions had appeared on the companions' faces.
They all knew there was no way such a plan could work. Several impossible obstacles stood in its way.
Lee Hyunsung, who had returned to the country thirty minutes earlier, spoke for the others.
“Sooyoung-ssi.”
Lee Hyunsung, who had hurried back to Korea on hearing about Yoo Joonghyuk and Han Sooyoung. A deep shadow lay over his eyes, which had always burned with justice and fighting spirit.
“We are tired. Now we are afraid of hope.”
Despair is not what truly wears a person out. It is hope that seems within reach yet never comes true, right to the end.
Han Sooyoung knew that, too. Her slowly curling fist tightened.
“I know. That's why I'm asking you.”
At the word 'asking', Lee Hyunsung's eyes wavered.
Han Sooyoung had never once used such an expression with him.
“I know the chances are low. So this is just······ a kind of ritual. Something I have to do to bring the past to a proper close, so I can somehow live the rest of my life.”
Jung Heewon asked.
“······What do you need us to do?”
Instead of answering, Han Sooyoung set a laptop on the small desk in the hospital room and opened a text file. The companions knew the file well.
A novel still titled 'Untitled'.
Slowly, Han Sooyoung typed that novel's title.
From that day on, Han Sooyoung began writing with the companions. Even she did not retain every memory intact, so she had to borrow theirs to complete the story.
“Get Dokja-ajusshi to read this novel······ But how do we make him read it?”
“It has to feel natural, without anything seeming off. So he doesn't even realize he's imagining this world.”
“Then we'll have to write a really fun story.”
“Didn't Dokja-hyung read even a boring novel to the end? Maybe he'd read it even if you just threw something together.”
Han Sooyoung shook her head at Lee Gilyoung's cheeky remarks.
“We should do our best, just in case. The Kim Dokja in another world might not be very patient.”
“I'll help, too!”
“Me, too! Noona, you don't know how teenagers talk these days, right?”
The novel was written mostly in Kim Dokja's hospital room. After teaching at school, Han Sooyoung visited his ward whenever she had time. The others took turns coming, too.
“Sorry I'm late. I have a presentation tomorrow―”
“You can help after you're done.”
“No way. Today's my awakening scene!”
Her voice was full of enthusiasm. Looking through Han Sooyoung's previous manuscript, Lee Jihye kept chattering.
“Wow, this part, seriously······ Ha, I really almost died here.”
“Ahh, this is amazing even on a reread. Unnie, is there maybe another scene with me······.”
“If you're going to keep interrupting, just leave.”
“Aw, why so cold? I even found a continuity error.”
“An error? Where?”
“I never said this!”
Lee Jihye pointed at the screen. Han Sooyoung glanced sideways at Lee Jihye's smartphone and spoke. Looking closer, she saw that it was a scene of Lee Jihye speaking in the Theatre Dungeon.
“Some adaptation is unavoidable, so it might differ a little from what happened. But that part······.”
「“How can you be alone? We're together! No, hold on······ I'm always by your side! Don't lose hope! Think of our child······!”」
“I wrote exactly what Uriel told me.”
One day, two, three. The sentences steadily accumulated.
When old memories would not come, she sometimes gave the sleeping Kim Dokja's cheek a long tug. When her resentment grew for no particular reason, she wrote strange things into the novel, too.
「“Find the Ugly King!”」
Well, it wouldn't matter. He wouldn't even know it was his own story.
The companions took turns visiting the hospital room as though coming to confession.
“Actually, I bad-mouthed Dokja-ssi a little here······.”
“Ah, don't write that down. Got it? ······I said don't write it.”
They seemed surprised they still remembered so many stories, and
“Noona! Sure, I respect hyung······ But how could you portray me as such a fanatic?”
they seemed comforted that they still remembered that story.
Sometimes they cried, or read through notes containing scattered thoughts about the stories still to be written.
Shin Yoosung asked.
“But why did you portray regression so negatively?”
“Kim Dokja only gets one life in that world. Reading this might influence him in a bad way. He might still be a kid.”
At Han Sooyoung's words, Shin Yoosung's expression darkened.
“But we regressed. Then should we write this part differently from what happened?”
“No. I'll write it as it is.”
“Huh? Why?”
“Because every human is a regressor.”

It was a sentence she had thought of while fighting Yoo Joonghyuk recently. Honestly, she had not expected Shin Yoosung to understand. Quietly considering the sentence, Shin Yoosung turned toward the view outside.

“Our regression had no effect on this worldline. Sometimes, when I think about it, it feels just like last night's dream. What's the difference between a past that couldn't change the present and a delusion that can't change anything?”
Slightly taken aback, Han Sooyoung opened and closed her mouth awkwardly. Shin Yoosung shrugged and smiled.
“What if you make it too complicated for Dokja-ajusshi to understand?”
“······Kim Dokja will understand.”
“You have more faith in ajusshi than you let on.”
“If you're going to interrupt, you can leave now.”
“I've put together an account of everything that's happened! Including the 'Disaster of Floods' you asked me about before······.”
Not everyone was as cooperative as Shin Yoosung. In fact, most of the time the companions only got in the way. Jang Hayoung, for example.
“Hey! You said I was the protagonist of Part Two! What's with my screentime? Are you kidding me?”
“It's just a figure of speech. You're not actually the protagonist.”
“Yeah, but still!”
“I'll write you a side story. A nice long one.”
“Deal.”
Pushing a hospital bed past them, Lee Seolhwa had something to say, too.
“In stories like this, healers usually end up as healbots.”
“······A Lee Seolhwa side story, too.”
Then there was Lee Gilyoung, who had skipped school to visit, and Lee Hyunsung, crying foul.
“You cut out everything I went through making a contract with Abaddon! And I've got so many skills, but with me it's always just cockroaches―”
“My stories about military service have been completely edited out! I explained it all so carefully, starting from when I was a private······!”
“All of you, stop! Kim Dokja is the protagonist of this story. It isn't your story.”
The constellations heard about Han Sooyoung and began visiting one by one, too.
For example, Uriel, armed with sunglasses and a mask and carrying an armful of mysterious documents.
[If you were writing something like this, you should have told me first. I've got this much material!]
“······Can I really trust this material? It's different from what Lee Jihye told me.”
[Well, a tiiiny bit might be wrong, but the universe is vast, and lots of Kim Dokjas live in lots of worldlines―]
Next came the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal.
[If you're writing about my Stories, you've at least read an unabridged translation of Journey to the West, right?]
“I read the comic.”
[Then you must know who the protagonist of Journey to the West is.]
“Isn't it Tang Sanzang?”
The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon.
[I'm disappointed. Did you forget my true name? It's already Part Two, so why is my true name still―]
“You never told me. And don't.”

By the time she had completed a first draft of more than 250 installments, Han Sooyoung was nearly collapsing from accumulated fatigue. Writing a novel had never been this hard. Many parts displeased her, and many needed revision. But for now, building up the word count came first. Because······.
―Han Sooyoung, it's this Saturday.
There was little time left.
Under normal circumstances, completing the first draft would have taken a little over two years, at the longest. But this worldline did not have that much time.
―The system is losing power too quickly. After this week, we might no longer have enough persuasiveness to launch the Ark.
In the end, Han Sooyoung decided to begin the first distribution when she finished the manuscript through Part Two.
At the news that the manuscript would finally go out, the companions were excited, too.
Yoo Sangah asked.
“How will you carry the file? A USB drive?”
“We'll prepare several methods······ But basically, it'll have to travel as a Story.”
“Who'll deliver it?”
“Me, obviously.”
“You can't. If you go, what about the Dokja-ssi here?”
Even if only a shell remained of Kim Dokja, he was still Kim Dokja.
If something happened to him while Han Sooyoung, who held the Bureau's Story, was away, his body might collapse. Yoo Sangah spoke.
“I'll go. I know the coordinates of the worldlines where Dokja-ssi reincarnated.”
Then Jung Heewon stepped forward to stop her.
“Sangah-ssi, you have to protect this place! I'll go. Give me the coordinates.”
“No! I'll go see hyung!”
“Obviously I should go. I'm ajusshi's incarnation!”
“No, as the foremost authority on the 'Demon King of Salvation', I······!”
With Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung, and even Jang Hayoung joining in, the place dissolved into chaos. Constellations and incarnations alike clamored to go.
Watching them, Yoo Sangah sighed.
“This isn't something to speak of so lightly. You all know crossing worldlines is dangerous, don't you?”
“Well, yes······.”
“If my tracking is correct, those worldline coordinates lie at the universe's outermost edge.”
“Outermost edge?”
“They might be worlds where 'scenarios' don't exist.”
No one knew what kind of worlds Kim Dokja had reincarnated in. Even their fundamental systems might differ from those of the Earth here.
“The system's protection could become far weaker than it is now. Naturally, skills and stigmas would weaken, too. And the journey won't be short.”
Listening, Anna Croft nodded, too.
She spoke as she watched the Ark on its test flight overhead.

“It was built for one person, so its equipment is not particularly good. Withstanding the backlash when crossing the Dark Fault will be especially difficult. It will take someone with tremendous mental strength. If something goes wrong, you could become an 'Outer God'.”
An Outer God. At those words, several companions' faces darkened. They remembered the 'Hounds Pursuing the Abyss' that had chased them.
And Anna Croft was not finished yet.

“There are also far too many worldlines where his soul has scattered. You may have to cross worldlines at least hundreds of thousands of times, perhaps millions or more······. Are you all prepared for that?”
Hundreds of thousands of times. Even at one worldline a day, that could mean a voyage lasting hundreds of years or more. Could anyone endure that much time without going mad, even for Kim Dokja?
“None of you can do it.”
Someone who could survive with the system's protection reduced to a minimum.
Someone who could face the rapids of unfathomable time without losing themselves.
And therefore, the person among them most likely to succeed in this mission.
“I will go.”
The passenger had already been decided.
At last, the day of the Final Ark's launch arrived.
Han Sooyoung watched Yoo Joonghyuk busily preparing to leave in the distance.
“I will not wear this crap.”
“Supreme King, you must. You are different now.”
It was a scene she wished she could show the Kim Dokja of five years ago. What would he think if she told him the prophet was looking after the regressor?
“You are truly a nuisance.”

“You say that now, but it will certainly help. Even Transcendents are not entirely free of the system's influence. Transcendents are beings established in opposition to the system. If it disappears, their power must gradually weaken, too.”
After glaring at Anna unhappily, Yoo Joonghyuk began putting on the equipment one piece at a time.
“This outfit hinders combat.”
“You are not going there to fight.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, looking fat in the thick spacesuit, was quite a sight. Han Sooyoung teased him.
“It suits you.”
“······Shut up.”
“Think carefully. Are you really going?”
Even now, just before departure, Han Sooyoung remained unsure.
「Was all this really necessary?」

This voyage was completely different from their regressions and worldline leaps until now. They would neither change the past nor seize the materials needed to open the [Final Wall] from another worldline.
This journey was, if anything, closer to a pilgrimage. A pilgrimage honoring the person they had searched for so long.
“Give me the manuscript.”
“You stopped regressing, but your damned manners haven't changed.”
With a sigh, Han Sooyoung opened her right hand. The power of the stigma she had developed swirled around her fingertips.
[The stigma 'Cloud System' is awaiting activation.]
A method similar to the way the [Fourth Wall] had once given Kim Dokja a file.
It was a stigma she had created by developing the power of [Predictive Plagiarism], which could communicate across worldlines, however unreliably.
“People with this stigma can share manuscripts. Making repeated round trips to Earth will be difficult, so I'll keep sending the manuscript through the cloud.”
“You expect me to learn your unique stigma? There is no time―”
“There isn't. But there's a way you can learn this one quickly. You don't have a sponsor now, right?”
At that moment, Yoo Joonghyuk realized what she meant.
“You are―”
“You think I like this?”
Frowning, Yoo Joonghyuk opened his Attributes Window.
When his stigma [Regression] disappeared, his sponsor disappeared with it.
Sponsor (背後星): None
He was now completely free.
“You expect me to take someone weaker than me as my sponsor?”
“I beat you last time.”
“I have no idea what nonsense you're talking about.”
“Want to go again?”
Still bickering as though neither would let the other have the last word, they finished signing the [Behind the Scenes Contract]. Both knew this was the best way.
[The constellation 'Architect of the False Last Act' has become the sponsor of the incarnation 'Yoo Joonghyuk'!]
[The incarnation 'Yoo Joonghyuk' has inherited the stigma 'Cloud System'.]
[The two beings' virtual clouds have been connected!]
“Never thought I'd live to see this day. I should tell that bastard Kim Dokja about it.”
“When I return, I will kill you and terminate our sponsorship contract first.”
“Try it if you can.”
With those final words, the two looked at one another for a moment.
“Remember. Never destroy another worldline. Just spread the story. So the Kim Dokja in that world can read it.”
“I know.”
“Don't die.”
“I will be back soon.”
He might never return.
They both knew that, but no one went out of their way to mention it. Except one person.
“Oppa.”
Tearfully, Yoo Mia clung to his spacesuit.
“Liar! You're not coming back! You won't be able to come back!”
“I will not die and leave you behind.”
Han Sooyoung held Yoo Mia's shoulders firmly as her tears kept falling. Slowly bending to meet his sister's eyes, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke gently.
“I promise. I will come back.”
Turning away, he sent Han Sooyoung a message.
―Take care of Mia.
After that, Yoo Joonghyuk boarded the [Final Ark] without looking back once. At Anna Croft's signal, its engine started.
The companions, who had heard the news late, watched it all.
The Ark slowly rising into the air. With the cockpit shut, their voices would not reach him inside.
Lee Jihye ran up, panting, and looked up at the Ark as it began to take off.
“Aren't you going to say goodbye?”
“If I say goodbye now, it'll feel like the last one.”
Despite her words, Lee Jihye's eyes already brimmed with tears. The others simply looked up at the Ark, saying nothing. Yoo Sangah spoke.
“Everything we want to say is in the novel. Joonghyuk-ssi will read it someday, too.”
“What does it matter if he reads it? What matters is hyung reading it.”
Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung, Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Jang Hayoung, Yoo Sangah, Lee Seolhwa, Lee Sookyung, Gong Pildu. And the constellations. Everyone watched the Ark fly. Shin Yoosung asked.
“Will Dokja-ajusshi really read our story?”
They did not know. Probably no one knew that. This operation was likely to fail, and Yoo Joonghyuk was likely to return empty-handed.
Their story might simply disappear as dust in a distant universe.
Yoo Joonghyuk must have known it as he left. Even so, he went. For himself. Or for the companions.
“If it's Kim Dokja, he'll read it.”
At least while waiting for Yoo Joonghyuk, the people here could live on, waiting for news of him.
“He promised me.”

The flames of the Ark as it leapt toward the galaxy. As though watching an exploratory vessel launched toward another alien world, the companions gazed endlessly after the receding Ark. The story written with their lives was vanishing beyond their reach.
[The 'Ark' enters the atmosphere.]
[Awaiting user Yoo Joonghyuk's destination setting.]
Yoo Joonghyuk entered the worldline coordinates Yoo Sangah had given him. Even the nearest lay unfathomably far away. As she had said, the 〈Star Stream〉 might not exist there.
[Dimensional acceleration begins.]
[Coins will substitute for part of the required energy.]

Coins collected from other worldlines were fed in as an energy source. Though they had lost value as the system weakened, they had once been this world's mightiest Story. Earth had already disappeared from sight.
[Passing through the Dark Fault for a worldline leap.]
Yoo Joonghyuk recalled Yoo Sangah's words.
―The worldlines where Dokja-ssi reincarnated are very far away. If you cross worldlines by ordinary means, there's no telling how long it will take.
The worlds where Kim Dokja had reincarnated lay outside 'Ways of Survival'. Entirely beyond this worldline's influence.
―You'll probably have to pass through a 'door' that lets you leap between worldlines.

How much time had passed? Things like bubbles began appearing ahead, one by one. The five-colored bubbles swelled and shrank in an ominous current. A faint, unsettling sensation. Yoo Joonghyuk knew where it came from.
Tsu-tsu-tsu-tsu-tsu······.

The Vice-King (副王) of the 'Outer Gods', and owner of the dimensional gate between worldlines. The being who had once opened the door to the 1863rd round for Kim Dokja. Yoo Joonghyuk swallowed without realizing it. Even after clearing every scenario, he felt tense before that power.
【You ······ are not the Plot ter】
A gigantic eye appeared through the sea of bubbles. Without looking away, Yoo Joonghyuk accelerated the Ark. To reach the outermost worldlines, he had to pass through there.
【That place is out side the sto ry】
“I don't care. Move, or I'll cut you down.”
Feeding all his Stories into it, Yoo Joonghyuk sent the Ark charging forward. The Vice-King did not particularly try to stop him. Instead, it merely spoke in a hollow voice.
【You who dream of what lies out side the dream the dream you dream can not come true】
The instant he struck the door, the view before him warped. Gritting his teeth, Yoo Joonghyuk endured the storm sweeping over him.
Savage sparks ate into his whole body. Holding back a scream, he suffered as though his entire body were being crushed to pieces.
―Can I ask one last thing?
Han Sooyoung's voice drifted through his dizzy mind.
―Why are you going so far to save Kim Dokja? You must have lost plenty of companions already.
―Losing many companions does not mean you grow used to loss. And······.
An explosion erupted inside the Ark. Fragments of broken equipment floated through space.
―There is something I must ask him.
Another roar sounded, and something pierced Yoo Joonghyuk's lungs.
[Failed to read worldline coordinates!]
[Warning! An error has occurred in the coordinate recognition device!]
[An error has occurred in the vessel's internal temperature controls!]
[An error has occurred in the vessel's navigation system!]
Sparks erupted in an instant and engulfed Yoo Joonghyuk's body. His vision went white, and he lost consciousness completely.
When he opened his eyes again, he was lost in the universe.
「Day 4 adrift.」
When he finally managed to regain his senses, Yoo Joonghyuk found a sharp fragment lodged in his abdomen. Calmly, he removed it and inspected the vessel.
「Day 6 adrift.」
He realized the Ark had completely ceased to function. Its navigation system was dead, and nothing was visible around him. Not even a nearby planet was visible.
「Day 11 adrift.」
As several of the Ark's built-in safeguards disappeared, things began to go wrong with his body, too.
[The system's homeostasis has broken down!]
[The power of Chaos erodes your entire body.]
[Your Stories are gradually collapsing.]
Something seemed to have gone wrong. All functions implemented through the system were paralyzed. Calmly, Yoo Joonghyuk checked his Stories. Fortunately, they were all intact.
[The Story 'Hell of Eternity' envelops you.]
The flames of hell protected his body from the cold.
「Day 21 adrift.」
The spacesuit Anna Croft had made him wear certainly helped. Without its built-in protection, his body would have deteriorated much faster.

Somehow, he repaired the Ark's power source. His work was hardly excellent, but the Ark began moving again. However, its reserve fuel tanks had exploded in the collision, so it now used his Story energy.
He could not repair the automatic navigation device or the autonomous piloting system. Now he had to pilot it himself.
「Day 34 adrift.」
Somehow, he had to find his route again.
「Day 42 adrift.」
As he continued to consume his Stories, fatigue gradually built up in his body. His lapses in consciousness grew longer. Darkness was gnawing at his mind.
······Why had he come all this way?
Sometimes his purpose blurred for a moment. He had come here to carry out a mission. To deliver a certain story to the reincarnated Kim Dokja. To revive the Kim Dokja the companions remembered.
Why? Because there was something he had to ask Kim Dokja.
······But what had it been?
「Day 58 adrift.」
His haggard face, reflected in the Ark's window. The moment he looked at it, Yoo Joonghyuk remembered the question he had forgotten.
―What should he live for in a world where the scenarios had ended?
Right. He had wanted to ask Kim Dokja that. The man had known everything.
Kim Dokja, who was always thinking of the end. Who planned everything, and did not hesitate to throw away his life to see a story's conclusion.
Someone like that seemed likely to know.
He had thought Kim Dokja might know him even better than he knew himself.
What did a regressor become once his regressions ended?
Lee Jihye had said she had nightmares every night.
For him, life had been a nightmare for a very long time. Even so, he could endure because there was still a goal he had not achieved. But that goal was gone now, and the scenarios were over.
Yoo Joonghyuk the regressor was free.
Yet faced with that freedom at last, he could not tell what he had gained in the end.
「Day 83 adrift.」
As he drifted longer, the Stories covering his skin dwindled rapidly. More and more of them scattered beyond the universe.
The voyage continued, but he did not know where he was going.
「Day 102 adrift.」
Yoo Joonghyuk began reading Han Sooyoung's novel.
He thought reading it might make this time a little easier to endure.
「Day 111 adrift.」
Reading Kim Dokja's story, Yoo Joonghyuk felt a faint hope.
Perhaps the Kim Dokja in this story could answer his question.
Starting from the first episode, he carefully read his way through Kim Dokja's life.
Some parts he knew, and others he did not. Certain sentences made him stop reading.

「The feeling of the protagonist and supporting characters walking into the sentence ‘And they lived happily ever after,’ leaving me alone beyond the story's final period. Amid the emptiness and sense of betrayal, my younger self struggled, unable to bear the loneliness.」

What was happiness? The word felt deeply unfamiliar to Yoo Joonghyuk. Perhaps he had known once. In his vague glimpse of zeroth-round memories, he thought he might have felt something like that. But that was no longer his life.
「Day 128 adrift.」
Kim Dokja, sustaining his life by relying solely on 'Ways of Survival', was unfamiliar to him. However often he read it, he could not quite understand.
How could a mere story sustain a life?
「Day 154 adrift.」
Gradually, Yoo Joonghyuk began getting used to reading novels.
There were passages he often reread, too.

「I took hold of the hind leg, glistening with just the right amount of fat, and tore off a whole piece of flesh. The juices gently seeping from the meat······ I closed my eyes, forgetting even to chew. Reading about something in a book really was different from tasting it myself.」

It was a scene where Kim Dokja and his companions, who had only just entered the scenarios, roasted and ate ground rat meat. Yoo Joonghyuk took jerky from the coat beneath his spacesuit and tore into it as he reread that passage. Slowly closing his eyes and chewing the meat, he felt as though the companions were together in the subway's damp darkness.
「Day 155 adrift.」
When he opened his eyes again, he was alone.
After staring blankly for a moment, Yoo Joonghyuk began reading again.
「Day 211 adrift.」
Alone, he kept reading that story, and
「Day 258 adrift.」
again, he read the story.
「Day 279 adrift.」
He came to understand Kim Dokja a little.
「Day 316 adrift.」
[Your Stories absorb your emotions.]

Whenever he read Han Sooyoung's story, his depleted Stories briefly regained their vitality. They could not recover as fast as they were consumed, but without reading this story, he could never have held out this long.
Still, he could not hold out like this forever.
The Kim Dokja in the novel was speaking.
「“See? You should have read to the end.”」
What did it really mean to read a story to the end?
He could not quite understand, but decided to follow that advice.
「Day 333 adrift.」
Suddenly, Yoo Joonghyuk realized why he was bound to fail.

「“Even if you save the world, you won't be saved. The moment you save it, the worlds you abandoned will come crashing down on you. Even if you save one world, all the other worlds you abandoned will drag you into hell.”」
Gazing into the distant universe, he thought.

What if this were his first or second round? If he had forgotten every memory of his previous lives. If he knew nothing of life in other rounds, could he have found an answer without wandering as he did now? Could he have avoided this suffering?
Could he have understood what a 'happy ending' meant, as in other stories?
Could he have lived to avoid dying?
Rrrrrumble.

The Ark's hull was shaking. Heightening his energy sense to find out what had happened, he felt a tremendous shock wave of energy sweeping in from behind. Hurriedly turning, he saw a host covering space in white. He knew these beings well, too.
【Oooooooooh······!】
Beings abandoned by worldlines and rejected by the scenarios.
An immense wave of 'Outer Gods' surged toward him in a mass. A faint smell of fear. Something was chasing them.
Crunch!
One of the 'Nameless Ones' at the rear was pierced through. What looked like at least several thousand 'Hounds Pursuing the Abyss' chased the 'Outer Gods' as though herding sheep.
Whenever a 'Nameless One' was hunted down, immense sparks erupted through the tidal wave. The energy storm kept growing. At this rate, he would be swallowed in an instant.
【Savemesavemesavemesavemesavemesaveme】
